title: Probabilistic prefetch strategy and TTL guardrails for KV/prefix caches
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Goal: Implement a probabilistic prefetch and TTL policy framework for KV/prefix caches that increases effective hit-rate for latency-sensitive endpoints while bounding unit-cost regressions. Deliverables: 1) hit-rate forecasting model that accepts per-prefix traffic histograms and returns recommended TTL ladders and prefetch probabilities; 2) a config schema and safe apply/rollback playbook (canary + shadow + circuit breaker) for runtime rollout; 3) monitoring/alerting thresholds and dashboards for automatic rollback triggers; 4) a small A/B experiment harness to validate cost vs latency tradeoffs at 1%-5% traffic slices. Motivation: Current static TTL policies under-serve bursty prefixes, resulting in higher per-token GPU cost and increased P50/P95 latency. Prior work focused on per-prefix TTL autottune but lacked probabilistic prefetch smoothing and explicit cost-safety gates. This ticket proposes a probabilistic prefetch layer that warms KV entries ahead of demand for a controlled fraction of requests, combined with a multi-ttl ladder to reduce cache churn and safe rollout controls.

Key concepts:
- Hit-rate model: mixture of exponential and Pareto components to capture short tails (session affinity) and long tails (cold prefixes). Use sliding-window frequency sketches plus reservoir sampling to infer time-to-next-hit distribution per-prefix.
- TTL ladder: compute [t_short, t_medium, t_long] where t_short addresses microbursts, t_medium captures typical session duration, and t_long prevents expensive recompute for moderately popular prefixes. Default ladder computed from quantiles (Q10, Q50, Q90) of the inter-arrival time distribution.
- Probabilistic prefetch: assign prefetch probability p(prefix) proportional to predicted probability of reuse within t_short but capped by a cost budget. Prefetch operations are issued asynchronously and attributed to a special prefetch metric for cost accounting.
- Safety gates: rollout uses shadowing, 0.1% canary, staged increases (0.1 -> 0.5 -> 1 -> 3 -> 10%) with guardrails on hit-rate delta, token-cost delta, and percentile latency. Automatic rollback triggers if any metric crosses configured thresholds for N consecutive minutes.
- Circuit breaker: if burst of prefetches causes backend saturation or LRU churn, open circuit for that prefix group and fall back to baseline TTL.

"Operational plan":
- Modeling: build offline simulator that replays 14 days of traffic from bigquery prefix logs and computes candidate ladders and p(prefix). Provide a cost delta table per candidate percentiles.
- Runtime: implement policy controller in the runtime config layer (supports per-prefix or per-prefix-group policies). Add feature flag gate and staged rollout API.
- Observability: add metrics: prefetch_count, prefetch_success_count, prefetch_latency_ms, cache_hit_rate_by_ttl, prefetch_cost_tokens, prefix_group_circuit_open, and derived KPIs: cost_per_request_delta, hit_rate_delta, pct_latency_impact.
- Experiment: instrumentation to run canary A/B with lineage metadata (policy_id) and pre-aggregated buckets for slide-window reporting. Playbook snippet and operator commands included below.

Playbook and rollback rationale: we constrain the first rollouts to policy candidates whose simulated cost_per_request_delta <= +2% while predicted hit_rate_gain >= +6% for target endpoints. Incremental rollout observes live metrics vs. shadow baseline. If hit_rate_gain < +3% OR cost_per_request_delta > +5% OR P95 latency increases by > 8% for 10m, rollback automatically to previous policy. The rollout plan permits manual override with documented steps for emergency rollback and postmortem.

Sample config template (yaml as string): """policy_id: prob-prefetch-v1
selector:
  prefix_group: "chat-session-affine"
  sample_rate: 0.01
ttl_ladder:
  short: 1s
  medium: 12s
  long: 120s
prefetch:
  enabled: true
  probability_p95_cap: 0.03
  cost_budget_per_min_tokens: 5000
safety_gates:
  hit_rate_delta_min: 0.03
  cost_delta_max: 0.05
  p95_latency_increase_max: 0.08
  consecutive_minutes_to_fail: 10
"""

Operator runbook (high level): 1) Deploy policy to shadow for 24h. 2) Validate prefetch_cost_tokens and prefetch_latency_ms are within expectations. 3) Create 0.1% canary and monitor metrics for 30m. 4) If metrics stable, continue staged increases. 5) On automatic rollback trigger: revert policy flag, mark circuit open for group, file incident and attach graphs. 6) Postmortem: compute where model assumptions failed and update simulator.dataset.

Success criteria:
- End-to-end hit-rate improvement >= 6% for targeted endpoints at <= +2% unit-cost increase in production after full rollout.
- No P99 latency regressions > 5ms attributable to policy.
- Ability to safely rollback within 5 minutes of trigger.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: prefetch amplifies load and causes backend spikes. Mitigation: enforce cost budget per-minute and overall prefetch_rate cap; queue prefetches into rate-limited workers.
- Risk: mis-modeled inter-arrival leading to wasted prefetches. Mitigation: conservative p caps, require 24h shadow validation, and use adaptive decay on p by observing realized hit probability.
- Risk: rollout complexity, operator confusion. Mitigation: provide clear UI state, automated rollback, and a prescriptive runbook with one-click revert.

Deliverables and timeline:
- Week 1 (this ticket): offline simulator and candidate policy generator; api + config schema; PR for runtime controller skeleton.
- Week 2: runtime controller implementation, metrics, shadow run.
- Week 3: canary rollout, automated safety gates, dashboards.
- Week 4: full rollout to target service groups with postrollout report.

Acceptance criteria:
- Simulator validated on heldout week and shows predicted hit-rate within +/- 10% of observed.
- Runtime accepts policy schema and policy_id appears in rollout audit logs.
- Automated rollback triggers at least once during test by running synthetic failure.

Long-term follow-ups (separate tickets):
- Integrate with autotune agent to propose p(prefix) daily and tighten ladders over time.
- Extend policy to multi-tenant priority weighting and quota-aware prefetch.
- Explore bloom-filter assisted pre-warm for large namespace prefixes to reduce prefetch cost.
